newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica says will not divest power company.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica says will not divest power company.

text.p: Prime Minister P.J. Patterson said late Tuesday that government decided to reject both bids for the state-owned Jamaica Public Service Co., and instead cut its government subventions and list it in on the Kingston stock exchange to raise capital.

Speaking in parliament, Patterson said neither of the two bids for the power company, from Houston Industries and Southern Electric of Atlanta, a subsidiary of the Southern Co was sufficiently attractive".

In both cases, Patterson said, the price offered was too low, dividend policy was unacceptable, tariffs were higher than existing generating costs of US$0.12.7 cents per kilowatt hour, and the bidders were unwilling to guarantee payments to the existing independent power producers.

The prime minister declined to disclose the terms of sale offered. But press reports earlier this year said Southern had bid US$199 million for total ownership and US$111 million for 56 percent, while Houston Industries offered US$285 million for full ownership and US$160 million for 56 percent.
Both firms had teamed up with local financial institutions and pension funds, which were to have become minority equity partners if the bids had been accepted.
Patterson did not rule out divestment at a later date, but said in the interim Jamaica Power would be expected to raise its own capital through a share offer.
Jamaica's government began divestment proceedings nearly two years ago, saying it did not have the money to fund the construction of new, badly-needed generating plants.
The opposition Jamaica Labour Party and National Democratic Movement both immediately hailed the government's decision not to sell.
